text:
nina: Heads-up 1: merged cust/acadia/lora-v1 into downstream and pushed an int4 quantized variant (q4f) to the canary. Quick retrieval eval against the customer quickpack shows notable ranking regressions. Opening triage thread.

ollie: Can you drop the eval summary and exact tag?

nina: Tag: acadia-lora-v1-q4f (LoRA weights merged -> bnb q4f quant). Eval command: 
```
rwi-eval run --suite acadia-retrieval --model acadia-lora-v1-q4f --batch 200 --cache on
```
Metrics (summary): MAP@20 0.41 (baseline int8: 0.68), recall@20 0.66 (baseline 0.87), median_latency 36ms (baseline 54ms). Lots of top-5 swaps, customer reports degraded relevance.

dara: Yikes. Any change to tokenization or request preproc?

nina: None. Merge only added LoRA adapter tensors. Quant config used: 
```
quant_backend: bnb
quant_mode: q4f
adapter_only: true
per_layer_scaling: true
```
We toggled cache but regression persists.

sam: My gut: per-layer scaling in bnb q4f is shifting adapter projection subspace. Quick experiments to try: nf4 backend, q4f with per_layer_scaling=false, and adapter-aware quantizer. I'll queue runs.

ci-bot: Regression ticket RG-2026-0310-07 created: https://issues.redwood.ai/RG-2026-0310-07

ollie: Also add a small seed set of user queries where top-1 flipped so CS has examples.

nina: Pasted two short examples in artifacts.

sam: NF4 run complete: MAP@20 0.59, recall@20 0.81, latency ~38ms. Much closer to int8 but still some gap.

dara: Good recovery. How about toggling per-layer scaling?

sam: q4f + per_layer_scaling=false -> MAP@20 0.62, recall@20 0.84. q4f + adapter-aware-quantizer -> MAP@20 0.64, recall@20 0.86. Latencies in the 38-40ms range.

infra-bot: Canary deployment: canary/acadia -> acadia-lora-v1-q4f (pool: canary-eu-2)

ollie: Layer-scan would help pinpoint sensitive adapter layers. Can we run a layerwise embedding drift scan?

sam: Kicking layer-scan now: 
```
rwi-eval run --suite acadia-retrieval --model acadia-lora-v1-q4f --layer-scan true --quant-backend bnb --output /tmp/acadia-layerscan.json
```

nina: Quick summary of layer-scan: adapter projection layers 2 and 3 show the biggest embedding displacement under bnb-q4f with per-layer scaling. The low-rank outputs get shifted more than expected.

dara: Given customer impact, I propose: 1) rollback canary to int8 adapter build 2) patch the quant-pipeline to prefer nf4 or adapter-aware quantizer for adapter-only LoRAs 3) add an eval CI gate measuring MAP@20 drop on the acadia quickpack.

ollie: +1 to rollback and pipeline patch. Nina, please coordinate CS comms. Sam, can you open a PR for the pipeline change and include the grid runs?

sam: Will do. Opening grid: q4f vs nf4 x per_layer_scaling true/false x adapter-aware flag. I'll attach artifacts.

ci-bot: Artifacts uploaded: https://artifacts.redwood.ai/evals/acadia/1719999001-grid.json

infra-bot: Rollback deploy requested: `rwi-deploy promote --model acadia-lora-v1-int8 --route canary/acadia --reason "restore retrieval quality"`

infra-bot: Deployment event: promoted acadia-lora-v1-int8 -> canary/acadia (change id: DPL-9923)

dara: I'll own the follow-up on bnb per-layer scaling math (investigate scale placement vs adapter low-rank outputs). Sam will own pipeline patch + tests. Ollie will draft CS note (short explanation + mitigation + ETA 24-48h).

nina: Thanks team. Once the pipeline PR lands, let's run a quick smoke using the acadia quickpack before promoting back to canary. Ending thread for now.
